title: Stored, Not Integrated: A Pre-Treatment Predictor and Three Controls for Knowledge Injection
description:
Fine-tuning stores new facts almost perfectly and leaves them unusable. In this work injected-fact recall is 1.000 while two-hop composition using the same fact is 0.22. This record contains the code, constructed datasets, results and manuscript behind a study of what determines which side of that gap a fact lands on — and whether it can be known before the fact is injected.

Version 0.2.0 corrects version 0.1.0. An independent review of the deposited code and data found errors in the analysis, including a confounded design behind the headline number. The confound was removed by re-running the experiment rather than by narrowing the claim, and the effect is larger in the corrected design. One of the five original contributions — a commit/defer gate — is withdrawn. All changes are listed in CHANGELOG.md in the repository.

Main findings

  • Composition is predictable in advance. A per-item measurement taken on the base model before any training predicts post-injection composition. With all 518 facts injected in a single adapter, so that the predictor's value cannot identify which model produced the answer, Spearman ρ = +0.362 over 518 items across three seeds (template-bootstrap CI [+0.204, +0.435]; template-stratified permutation p = 0.0001), positive within five of five testable templates.
  • It is not a restatement of bridge-entity familiarity. Controlling for how well the base model already knows the bridge entity attenuates the association but does not remove it (+0.362 to +0.219).
  • Training explicit first-hop generation did not improve chaining. Raising bridge-entity generation from 0.000 to 1.000 yields no gain over a control that trains an unrelated fact.
  • Much of the "supply the intermediate" benefit is truth-insensitive. Supplying the bridge in context raises composition from 0.220 to 0.498, but a false-bridge control shows a quantity equal to about 68% of that gain is followed regardless of whether the bridge is correct.
  • A published self-patching recovery figure is measured against the wrong baseline. On an uninjected model the per-item maximum of the same statistic is +0.80 — a maximum over many null comparisons is positive by construction.

Negative results and withdrawals are included, not omitted. An intervention derived from the diagnosis did not beat a data-diversity control, and a test of template generalisation did not reach significance despite a design change intended to secure it. Interpretations adopted during the project and later overturned are recorded with the evidence that overturned them, as is the commit/defer gate withdrawn in this version.

Contents. Dataset construction by graph traversal over PrimeKG/STaRK-Prime; LoRA injection, evaluation and every reported analysis; per-item evaluation output for all runs; the manuscript with ten figures, as Markdown source and a built PDF. Every figure regenerates from the deposited JSON with a single command and no GPU. Model checkpoints (~7 GB) and the source knowledge graph are not redistributed; the construction scripts take the graph as input.

Setup. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with LoRA (r=16, α=32) over biomedical relations from PrimeKG, three seeds. Base-model weights are pinned to explicit revisions; the pin binds runs made from this version onward, and 2 of the 23 deposited run manifests record it while 21 predate it and record the model name only. One recorded dataset hash does not match its deposited file, for a documented and verified-equivalent reason; see the repository README. The primary design injects all 518 facts, spanning both signs of the predictor, in a single adapter; an earlier separate-adapter design is retained for the within-condition experiments and reported alongside it.
